newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Nafta Polska adopts oil privatisation plan.
newsitem.headline: Polish Nafta Polska adopts oil privatisation plan.

text.p: Oil holding group Nafta Polska SA adopted a privatisation strategy saying foreign firms can only get access to Poland's existing fuel distribution network through investment in its refineries, Rzeczpospolita said.

The daily reported on Saturday that this condition was among principles confirmed on Friday by the board of Nafta Polska, created in May to manage and restructure the sector before it opens to foreign competition in the next few years.

"This clause rules out the possibility the (state-owned) CPN SA retail network can be opened to those oil firms which do not invest in development of crude oil refining in Poland," the newspaper said.

Such firms would only remain on the market through their own networks or deals with private firms, while those investing in refineries would be able to make lucrative use of the CPN chain, which is to join Nafta Polska by the end of 1996.
The Nafta board decision on CPN conforms with the government's scheme for the industry's privatisation.
Nafta sees privatisation of the seven oil refineries, which may be less attractive to investors than the distribution system, as its most urgent task.
It plans to sell between 20 and 30 percent stakes of two groups of refineries, to be set up around the two biggest which are based in the cities of Plock and Gdansk.
Investors in the refineries would later be able to extend their stakes and Nafta Polska itself would eventually be privatised.

Last month, CPN's president said it was preparing its own privatisation programme in case the government scheme was not implemented if, for example, investors proved not to be interested in buying refineries and CPN jointly.
CPN runs nearly 1,400 of Poland's 4,700 petrol stations. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
